messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — saw a tenant-level starvation case after switching to `fastpath_v3` on C4 nodes, long sequences dropping throughput hard. KV hit-rate also dropped.
Maya: which rollout/flag? `kernel=fastpath_v3` was toggled last night?
Alex: yes, rolled last night to optimize short requests. Microtrace shows shortrequests favored, longqueue growth. attaching a tiny trace snippet.
Tony: paste the sample logs?
Alex: here's the minimal snippet:
```
# tracer snippet
t=0 tenant=acct-42 seq_len=1024 admit=0.4 tokens_req=1024
t=5 kernel=fastpath_v3 assigned batch=3
t=6 longqueue=+8 shortqueue=-5 token_budget[acct-42]=-800
```
Li: that token_budget spike negative is the smoking gun. Fastpath greedily consumes microbatch credits and doesn't respect a per-tenant floor.
Maya: proposal: implement an "epochal-zigzag" credit router — alternate credit drains between long and short windows every N seconds, plus enforce a tenant token floor: tenant_floor = max(ceil(avg_seq * alpha), min_floor)
Sam: what's alpha and min_floor? numbers?
Maya: start alpha=0.5, min_floor=128 tokens. Also add `long_target_ratio=0.3` in admit policy so longs get at least 30% of token budget over epoch.
Tony: we should also address KV behavior — long sequences more likely to miss due to cold prefixes. Consider prefetch-on-accept for long batches.
Alex: agree. Can we canary this on a small cohort in prod-dedicated?
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by Alex: canary/epochal-zigzag -> pool=prod-dedicated-a4 rollout=5% (started)
Maya: add tracepoints: `kv.hits_per_token`, `kernel.selection`, `per-tenant.token_budget`.
Li: also add a demotion/backpressure rule: if tenant token_budget < -512 then demote that tenant's traffic to slowpath until budget recovers.
Sam: demoting sounds safe, but watch short p99 impact.
Tony: slowpath increases short p99 by ~30-50ms in earlier tests but stops starvation. Another idea: prefer slowpath when batch contains >1 long seq.
Alex: I'll run a 24h replay simulation with the new admit config. Config draft:
```
admit:
  long_target_ratio: 0.3
  tenant_floor_tokens: 128
  tenant_alpha: 0.5
  demote_threshold: -512
kernel:
  fastpath_v3:
    prefer_short: true
  slowpath_v2:
    fallback_on_demote: true
kv:
  prefetch_on_accept: true
  prefetch_window: 64
```
Maya: run sim and post CSV with fairness metric: median_latency_long / median_latency_short, and kv-hit delta.
Alex: kicking off local sim now. ETA ~12m.
Tony: quick note — if you see oscillations add credit refill smoothing: `ema_window=30s`.
Li: +1. Also capture `token-budget-oscillation-rate` telemetry.
deploy-bot: canary health update: 5% traffic, initial 30s probe passed
Alex: sim result (first pass): long/short median ratio improved from 4.2 -> 1.6, KV-hits +2.3%, short p99 +22ms. Uploaded CSV and traces: https://drive.redwood.internal/sim/epochal-zigzag/3567890123.csv
Maya: tradeoff looks acceptable. Next step: 20% rollout for 2h, collect per-tenant fairness and SLA checks.
Sam: rollback criteria: any tenant throughput drop >10% or any SLA breach in p95 latency.
Tony: will run A/B with a kernel selection tweak — threshold on seq_len=256 instead of alpha param.
Li: I'll add unit tests covering token_budget underflow and demote logic.
Alex: follow-ups: PR for admit config, sim dashboard, ops runbook for rollback. I'll open the PR after tests pass.
Maya: assigning action items: Alex -> PR + sims, Li -> tests, Tony -> A/B kernel experiment, Sam -> monitor run, Maya -> dashboard + telemetry.
Sam: noted. ping me if canary shows surprises.
Alex: thanks everyone. We'll circle back after the 20% roll.
